1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Be7 4.Bc4 Bh4+ 5.strategy: Offers a pawn to hit the bishop: Black simply takes it and is two pawns up, and White's open lines are not worth that much against accurate defence. A speculative gambit, so Black is better with best play.
1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Be7 4.Bc4 Bh4+ 5.name: King's Gambit Accepted: Cunningham Defence, Bertin Gambit
1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Be7 4.Bc4 Bh4+ 5.background: Also called the Three Pawns' Gambit, it was played in the nineteenth century.

1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Be7 4.Bc4 Bh4+ 5.strategy: Takes the pawn, which removes the attacker of the h4-bishop and puts Black two pawns up; the pawn on g3 also attacks h2. White has open lines and quick development for the pawns, so Black has to defend carefully, but the extra material is real.
